briefings.headline: Be ready for Scherzer’s fastball—and make him work
briefings.message: Max Scherzer is the medium-confidence starter prediction. Hunt strikes, especially fastballs; lefties should be ready for his fastball group, and righties should avoid expanding against breaking balls. Dominic Canzone and Cal Raleigh have batter edges; Cole Young should look for breaking balls. Stay patient and be prepared for Toronto’s bullpen: Scherzer averages 4.2 innings per start.
reminders: J.P. Crawford: hunt fastballs; lay off breaking balls outside the zone.
Raleigh: sit fastball and be selective against offspeed.
Patrick Wisdom is a late option against a left-handed reliever; his Scherzer matchup results are small sample.

briefings.headline: Change looks, keep the ball off the middle
briefings.message: Logan Gilbert starts; target six innings with a 95-pitch limit. Use splitter and changeup to lefties, and lean on breaking balls to Vladimir Guerrero Jr. Keep fastballs unpredictable to Guerrero Jr. and Alejandro Kirk. If the game stays close late, use rested leverage arms first and save Andrés Muñoz for the final inning; bring in the relievers limited after yesterday’s work only if needed.
reminders: Attack Ernie Clement and Andrés Giménez early.
Use Gabe Speier as the first left-handed setup choice; monitor Seranthony Domínguez’s workload.
Use Michael Rucker for length, monitoring his recent workload.

briefings.headline: Execute the Scherzer matchup; preserve late leverage
briefings.message: The approved lineup follows the medium-confidence Max Scherzer prediction, with Cal Raleigh, Julio Rodríguez, and Randy Arozarena starting despite rest suggestions. Scherzer averages 4.2 innings per start, so prepare for Toronto’s bullpen. Logan Gilbert’s target is six innings with a 95-pitch limit. Keep the limited relievers—Eduard Bazardo, José A. Ferrer, and Carlos Vargas—in reserve unless needed; prioritize rested high-leverage arms in close late innings.
reminders: Use Victor Robles for a late tying or go-ahead run, or as a corner-outfield defensive replacement—not both.
Use Jhonny Pereda if Raleigh needs to leave.
Patrick Wisdom’s matchup edge relies on small samples; consider him against a left-handed reliever in a key at-bat.
